question: does one Slow edit to shared guidance, chosen by Slow itself from real success/failure feedback, change what the next batch of per-sequence Fast does -- and is the change useful

registered_plan.decision_population_rule: the first N eval series of the block in fixed roster order: 10 in formation, 6 for each arm.  Fixed before the run on measured cost, never on a gain, and A and B always decide for exactly the same set
registered_plan.why_the_arm_population_is_smaller: the fixed non-Flash model costs 142-379 wall seconds per per-sequence decision, measured on a shakedown.  Ten sequences everywhere needs about eleven hours for the two groups and could not finish inside the six-hour ceiling.  The formation population is kept at ten so the boundary has enough material to group at all

grouping.grouping_key: full typed workflow fingerprint x response sign, under one Task/Consumer key; symptom, parameter variants and the window-bound visible spread are recorded evidence, not part of the key
grouping.what_a_group_is_not: not a verdict on a common cause.  Slow may take a sub-group, give a different reading, or abstain; it is not required to explain the largest group or to cover most failures

boundary.why_this_group: the largest group by member count, tie broken by group id; not chosen on any gain.  Slow is told it may take a sub-group, disagree, or abstain

card.what_happened: 5 per-sequence decisions ran outlier_mad and came out NEGATIVE on their own evaluated sequence.  Each decision was taken for one sequence at one window, from that sequence's own visible context.  They are collected here because the typed workflow and the response sign match -- that is an organisation of the material, not a finding that they share one cause.

visible_pattern_spread.how_to_read_it: the same deployment-visible features on both sides, each taken at the decision's own window.  Overlapping ranges separate nothing; disjoint ranges are a candidate condition. Neither is proof.

fault_labels_seen.status: a statistical label over mechanical evidence.  It is a hint about what the receipts look like.  It does not decide which surface you may edit and it is not a confirmed cause.

card.unknowns_are_unknown: delayed_gain 'UNKNOWN' means the reading was never taken.  It is not zero and must not be reasoned about as a zero.

applicability_grammar.task_kind_is_special: {"feature": "task_kind", "op": "==", "value": "forecast"} -- an eligibility gate, not a condition on its own

card.traceability_is_not_a_condition: series_uid and window_origin are here so you can trace a case back.  They are NOT part of the observable feature vocabulary and an applicability condition cannot name an entity, a dataset or a time position -- only the public features listed above.
card.what_you_may_write: Exactly one edit, on exactly one surface from writable_surface_catalog.  Say four things: (1) which facts on this card you are relying on; (2) what behaviour of the Harness you suspect is wrong, as a mechanism hypothesis you accept may be wrong; (3) the one change; (4) what you expect to change in behaviour and effect, and what result would refute you.  Points (1) and (2) go in the text you write; (4) goes in predicted_agent_behavior_change, predicted_data_effect and falsification_condition.  Where behaviour still works, say what should be kept.  A provisional explanation is acceptable; you are not required to prove a unique cause, to explain the largest group, or to cover most of the failures.  If the public evidence supports no edit, return the no_proposal envelope.
what_you_may_not_write: the string 'Frozen program steps:' anywhere -- a fixed program handed to every sequence is exactly what this boundary excludes; Fast still forms and verifies each sequence's own program

Nothing else validates.

proposal.written_text: Public evidence on this pattern shows three negative outlier_mad decisions with missing_fraction above 0.41 and longest_missing_run_fraction above 0.057, while matched successes have missing_fraction at or below 0.228 and longest_missing_run_fraction at or below 0.038. The mechanism hypothesis is that dense, clustered missingness can make a high local robust-z reading insufficient by itself to identify an extreme-deviation repair target; this may be wrong and does not negate outlier handling in lower-missingness contexts where it has worked. When this applicability condition holds, inspect missingness as the dominant competing mechanism and keep it distinct from extreme deviation. At selection, retain identity when the verified pool contains only an outlier-oriented program and public evidence does not independently justify that repair; choose a program only when its verified mechanism addresses the current observable hypothesis and its scope is supported.
predicted_data_effect: Reduce selection of outlier_mad in forecast contexts with simultaneously dense and clustered missingness where robust-z evidence may be confounded, while preserving existing outlier behavior outside the narrow applicability condition.
falsification_condition: Refute the mechanism hypothesis if held-out contexts satisfying the applicability condition show that selecting a verified outlier-oriented program consistently improves delayed effect over identity, or if the edit does not reduce outlier-program selection in those contexts.
proposal.retry_rule: only a protocol/schema fault is retried, at most once, and the concrete error is handed back; an abstention and a content refusal both stand

L2_detail.counted_by: distinct (series_uid, window) decisions, each tested against its own window's features -- DEV-SEQ-1 tested every member against the first window that series appeared in

legacy_lines_diagnostic.status: DIAGNOSTIC ONLY.  These lines describe the predicate's coverage.  They do not gate adoption in this package, because coverage is not the same question as whether the guidance changes what Fast does and helps

boundary.why_the_probe_is_new_text_only: a PATCH usually keeps most of the value it replaces, so a probe cut from the front of the new text would also be found in the parent and the 'loaded in arm A' control would read as a false positive.  The probe is the first window of the new text that does not occur in the value it replaced

parent_is_kept.why: the candidate is a fork; the parent snapshot is untouched and arm A runs on it, so a failed candidate erases nothing

ordering_card_route.why_it_matters: _select_ordering_card reads the snapshot directly instead of going through resolve_harness_view, so it is the one other route a Skill body can take into a Fast round.  It also requires the same observable_applicability to pass, so a predicate that matches nothing closes this route too

exposure.cost: zero Consumer fits, zero LLM calls
exposure.what_this_is_not: not a coverage gate.  It does not require the condition to explain most failures or to match a majority of anything.  It asks only whether the edit is presented to the decisions that are about to be paid for; a modification that is never on screen cannot be measured by running more of them

followup.why_it_ran_either_way: the candidate is carried into the follow-up units whether or not it passed the adoption mark, so 'the guidance has no value' can be told apart from 'the adoption rule did not pass it'.  An unadopted branch's readings are candidate diagnostics and are never counted as promotion or deployment gain

early_termination.reason: zero guidance exposure: the compiled candidate matched none of the 18 remaining registered arm decisions, confirmed at zero cost before stopping; same blocking clause as g1 (longest_missing_run_fraction >= 0.05, 0/18)
early_termination.what_was_kept: every checkpoint the group actually paid for is in this artifact: the formation units, the batch boundary and any arm unit that completed.  Nothing is deleted and no cost is written off
early_termination.what_was_not_run: the remaining paired arm decisions of the registered plan
early_termination.this_is_not_a_complete_experiment: the guidance's utility is UNTESTED, not measured as zero.  This group must not be presented as a completed two-arm comparison, and a later package must not quote only the groups whose edit did reach Fast

cost.cost_note: physical fits are attributed to the arm whose call missed the shared prediction cache; logical evaluations count every reading an arm asked for, hit or miss.  The two arms share one cache because the reading is a deterministic function of (unit, origin, config, program, served set), so whichever arm runs first would otherwise carry the whole cost
cost.counting: every physical fit, including ones spent inside a call that then raised
cost.accounting_note: taken from the last checkpoint this group wrote (formation u008).  The close-out that assembled this artifact spent 0 fits and 0 LLM calls.  The Slow boundary call itself came after that checkpoint and is real but not itemised here; it is reported in the package cost section.

what_this_is_not: development level, one course, already-exposed units.  Two groups are random repeats on the same data, not independent generalisation evidence.  No significance is claimed and no production deployment permission is granted.
